invariant_owner_layer.why: The shared submission ledger distinguishes unacknowledged creates from rejections; captured asset contexts prevent a delayed result from changing project identity.

problem_type: Execution-contract drift during stable upstream integration
symptom: An accepted asynchronous create without a remote task ID appeared as a retryable failure; custom generated outputs could miss the fixed project publication context.
direct_cause: The upstream missing-ID branch returned a failed DTO with a local fallback ID, while custom execution paths were not yet migrated to the new publication context.
class_root: A transport response without an acknowledgement is not evidence of rejection, and a delayed local output cannot re-resolve its destination after execution.
affected_population: GUI and capability submissions sharing an intent
Codex image output during project identity replacement
entry_points: Persistent task recovery and free queries
internal_only_reason: The invariants are local application contracts. Both official v0.23.2 source and the customized snapshot are available in the integration repository.
invariants: A missing remote acknowledgement never becomes proof of a safe resubmission.
Repeated intent keys coalesce before node exclusivity and survive restart without creating again.
Delayed image output is published only through its captured project identity.
Query reconstruction carries the explicitly requested project to process operations.

door_reduction.why_not: The desktop assembly injects one shared task runtime; the IPC registrar retains a factory default for isolated hosts and tests. Both construct the same idempotency-before-node-exclusivity implementation.

generality_proof: The shared submission runtime owns replay for both desktop callers, and the canonical runtime checks all asynchronous create acknowledgements before admitting a task. Captured asset contexts validate identity immediately before writing.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: One idempotent submission and query-only recovery owner.
Never synthesize a failed remote task from an unacknowledged create.
Capture the destination before spending and publish through that context.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both capability run and renderer registration receive the same runtime instance.
The default host and injected desktop instance use createTaskSubmissionRuntime.

recurrence.reason: Any asynchronous provider or restarted host may omit an acknowledgement or replay a paid intent.
same_class_scan: Reviewed runtime runTask, taskResultQuery rebuildCachedTaskFromPayload, and Codex publication
Independent reviewer 01a15742-6323-7fa3-a4c1-bed6d3583260 reproduced both execution classes without network

prevention.invariant: The submission ledger records unknown outcomes and never automatically repeats create for a persisted intent.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing acknowledgement throws the structured submission-unknown code; stale publication contexts reject before write.
prevention.strategy: Keep one task-submission owner and the official asset-write context rather than provider-specific retry fallbacks.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove the branch that cached a fabricated failed task ID after an unacknowledged create; no active-project fallback is restored.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Receipt classification and project identity are application invariants, not dependency behavior.

migration: Existing project contents are not rewritten. Old persisted intent records remain fail-closed; new unacknowledged submissions are recorded as unknown without a fabricated provider ID.
residual_risks: Real paid provider generation is deliberately not exercised in this merge.
